Empires & Puzzles Theobald Review: Is The Miracle Bear Worth It?

Is Theobald just a cute bear with knives, or does he have bite? Our deep dive analyzes his slow mana, unique Green Reflect mechanic, and whether this Starfall Circus ringmaster can still perform in today's fast-paced meta.
Theobald Review: The Knife-Throwing Miracle Bear
Theobald: The Knife-Throwing Bear Who Brings a Gun to a Knife Fight (Eventually)
Theobald is a 5-star Legendary Ice hero from the

family, released back in 2021. In an era where heroes were starting to get complicated, Theobald decided to do... everything. He hits, he buffs, and he reflects. He's a "Jack of All Trades, Master of None," except in one very specific niche where he reigns supreme. If you like bears with monocles and throwing knives, you're in the right place. Just don't expect him to move very fast—he is a hefty bear, after all.

Theobald is arguably one of the most dapper designs in the game. He's a massive, anthropomorphic bear sporting a fine coat, a monocle (or at least a very fancy expression), and... well, he's holding throwing knives like he's about to perform a magic trick that might go wrong. The Starfall Circus aesthetic is strong here, mixing a bit of whimsy with a threat of violence. It's a fantastic character design that screams "I run this show," even if his mana speed screams "I'm taking a nap."

Family Bonus, Passives, Aether Power & Unique Abilities

The Starfall Circus family bonus provides a chance to cleanse status ailments at the end of the turn. It's a nice passive safety net, especially since Theobald is slow and vulnerable to ailments like Silence or Mana Control before he can fire. However, relying on a 40-60% chance is risky strategy.
Theobald does not have innate passives beyond the family bonus, a hallmark of his older design.

Upon release, Theobald was a niche pick. Players compared him to Ursena and Mitsuko (Elemental Reflectors) but lamented his Slow speed. He was seen as a counter to the Frigg/Odin meta, but often too slow to work.
The stat gap is undeniable. His damage is no longer threatening. His primary value has shifted entirely to
tournaments and wars, specifically to counter Green-heavy defenses (especially those with Alibrand or heavy green AoE hitters). Outside of Rush, he is largely too slow and fragile for top-tier play.
Theobald needs to survive to fire. Period. His damage is secondary to his utility.

Many players initially felt the Attack Buff was "slapped on" to justify his Slow speed.

"I would really hate to miss Theo if he was average speed. Now as he’s slow, I am fine passing on him." - This sentiment from his release still holds true; at Average, he would be broken. At Slow, he is balanced to the point of being niche.

Theobald is a relic of a different time, dressed in a fancy suit. He is not a daily driver for raids, nor is he a defense team staple anymore. However, in the specific chaos of

, he transforms from a sluggish bear into a terrifying ringmaster. The ability to reflect all Green status effects—including defense down and mana drain—is a unique utility that keeps him relevant even as his stats age. Keep him for the 5% of the game where he is absolutely essential, and let him rest in his circus tent for the other 95%.
